value.rationale: The complete reset-attempt count is a natural cost of stochastic searching, separate from first-passage time moments. Two noncancelling modes reveal persistent-gate memory, and a slow-gate exponential limit gives an exact experimentally relevant distributional scale for initially closed targets. Both exact count law and sharp scaling carry information not reported by the motivating source's mean/FPT theory.
